title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC panel declared Complaint 2010-01 abandoned because Mr. McNeil failed to appear for the hearing, then dismissed the case because it was abandoned; no merits ruling was made.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed Michael McNeil's appeal against Chesapeake Presbytery after he failed to appear for the hearing. Notice had warned that nonappearance would abandon the appeal. The case was declared abandoned and dismissed.
summary: Michael McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery was dismissed without a merits ruling after McNeil failed to appear at the SJC hearing. The panel called his name outside the hearing room and the Stated Clerk’s office; he was absent and had filed no brief. The notice had warned under BCO 42-11 that an appellant’s failure to appear would be treated as abandonment. The SJC declared the case abandoned and dismissed it. This illustrates dismissal for nonappearance, not adjudication of the underlying complaint.

sources.supports: Caption, hearing nonappearance, BCO 42-11 notice, abandonment and dismissal motions, adopted vote, and disqualification note.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Caption at line 11 identifies Complaint 2010-01, Mr. Michael McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery. The adopted vote appears at lines 29–33: 18 concurring, 1 disqualified, 5 absent.
evidence_notes.dispute: The panel met June 7, 2011, for the hearing. McNeil’s name was called outside the hearing room and outside the Stated Clerk’s office; he was not present and had submitted no written brief (lines 13–19).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The panel moved and carried that the case be considered abandoned because McNeil was not present, then moved and carried that because it was abandoned the case be dismissed (lines 21–23). No merits reasons are stated.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The hearing notice warned under BCO 42-11 that failure to appear would cause the appellant to be considered to have abandoned the appeal (lines 15–18). TE Meyerhoff was disqualified under OMSJC 2.10(e) and 2.10.d(3)ii because he was a member of a presbytery that is a party to the case (lines 35–38).
